_readme: Regions for scripts/verify/night-refmeasure.py: the rectangles on the WEB REFERENCE PHOTOGRAPHS that docs/night-reference-package.md §5 and docs/night-implementation-plan.md §7.2 A1 quote ratios from. Until 2026-09-20 nobody had measured a web photo (the package says so itself, §7: 'Nobody measured the web photos'), so A1's 'unlit wall / horizon sky <= 0.5 at blue hour' came from looking at them. This file is the regions; the photographs themselves live outside the repo in austin-reference-images/_night/ and are never committed.
_units: x0,y0,x1,y1 as FRACTIONS of the image, like night-routes.json. Ratios are medians of linear relative luminance (sRGB decoded), the same unit night-compare.mjs divides with.
_caution: A camera exposes to make a scene legible; it does not measure it. Two photographs of the same sky at the same minute, at different ISO/shutter, give different sRGB codes. A RATIO of two regions inside ONE frame survives that (both regions moved together). An ABSOLUTE sRGB level from a web photo does not, and §5's ladder must never be read off one.

photos.regime: sunset (sun -2.6 deg from its own 20:34 stamp, NOT blue hour)
photos.note: 20:34 on 2012-07-31, seven minutes after sunset: the sun is -2.6 deg, so this is the top of civil twilight, not blue hour. wall = the Austonian's dark glass shaft above the lit chevrons; the first rectangle tried here sat on a pale concrete face still catching the western afterglow and read wall/sky 2.16.
19:08 panorama across the lake. Distant skyline: no broad unlit wall, so this frame answers water/sky only.
Lamp head in frame top-left; the sky rectangle is kept clear of its flare.
06:51 dawn twilight, optically the dusk blue hour reversed.

photos.regime: deep night (NOT blue hour - see note)
photos.note: Kept as the entry that disproves its own tag. sources.json tags it 'blue hour (pre-dawn twilight)' and night-routes.json bound it to congress-street/blue AND capitol/blue. Its sky measures median linear Y 0.0011, sRGB code 3 - black. Its camera clock says 2019-08-11 06:06 (sun -10.8 deg, nautical twilight, a sky that is not black); the photographer's own caption says 5AM (sun about -21 deg, a sky that is). The pixels and the caption agree and the clock is wrong: this is deep night, and it was sitting on two blue rows.
The one West Campus street frame at blue hour. Wall = the red brick low-rise on the left, which carries no light of its own.

Tagged 'blue hour / early night'; no time is stated, and the sky still carries colour while every tower is fully lit, so it is late blue hour at the earliest. wall = the dark upper shaft of the triangular-crowned tower on the left. The first rectangle tried here sat on the lit Radisson facade.

photos.regime: sunset (NOT twilight - see night-routes.json wc-street refNote)
photos.note: Measured 2026-09-20 to settle what regime it is: direct orange solar glow on the right horizon, pink-lit cirrus, a bright blue zenith and a fully legible facade. It is a sunset frame, ~12 deg off the nautical-twilight row it used to sit on.
